import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 898

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/898](https://www.erdosproblems.com/898)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Mordell_inequality)
-/

open Affine EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos898

/--
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

Conjectured by Erdős in 1932 (according to [Er82e]) and proved by Mordell soon afterwards, now
known as the Erdős-Mordell inequality.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos898.lean"]
theorem erdos_898 (A B C P L M N : ℝ²) (hABC : AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C])
    (hP : P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set ℝ²)))
    (hN : N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]) (hPN : line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction)
    (hM : M ∈ line[ℝ, B, C]) (hPM : line[ℝ, P, M].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, B, C].direction)
    (hL : L ∈ line[ℝ, C, A]) (hPL : line[ℝ, P, L].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, C, A].direction) :
    dist P A + dist P B + dist P C ≥ 2 * (dist P M + dist P N + dist P L) := by
  sorry

end Erdos898

reformulations.difference: The Lean characterizes each perpendicular foot using membership in a supporting affine line and orthogonality of direction subspaces, and universally quantifies over these feet. It expresses a nondegenerate triangle using affine independence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The direction of line[ℝ, P, N] is the span of P − N. Thus N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B] together with direction orthogonality is equivalent to N being the orthogonal projection of P onto line[ℝ, A, B]. Such a foot exists uniquely, so universally quantifying over the three feet is equivalent to the usual inequality involving perpendicular distances to the three supporting lines. Wikipedia explicitly permits feet outside side segments in obtuse triangles. AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C] is equivalent to noncollinearity. The full equivalence with the noncollinear/projection-distance formulation was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as reviewed_statement_iff_projection_statement, without relying on the reviewed theorem's sorry.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved (1982), §I.1, p. 61: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, including non-vacuity, repeated vertices, zero line directions, foot existence/uniqueness, and exact Euclidean-distance tests.
